Boil the following paragraph down to a single sentence:

'Permafrost underlies nearly a quarter of the land in the Northern Hemisphere. As the climate warms, this frozen ground thaws unevenly, buckling roads, cracking building foundations, and tilting pipelines across Arctic towns. The thaw also releases carbon dioxide and methane that were locked in frozen organic matter for thousands of years, which in turn accelerates the warming that caused the thaw. Engineers now cool the ground beneath critical structures with thermosiphons, while climate researchers warn that emissions from thawing ground remain absent from most national carbon budgets.'

expected_answer.summary: Thawing permafrost is damaging Arctic infrastructure and releasing long-stored greenhouse gases that speed further warming, prompting engineering fixes and warnings that these emissions are missing from national carbon budgets.

Write a three-sentence overview of this report for a busy executive:

'The 2026 Battery Recycling Market Review surveys collection and processing capacity across North America and Europe. Recycled lithium output doubled in 2025 as four large hydrometallurgical plants came online, and recovered materials now meet 9 percent of regional battery-grade demand. Collection remains the bottleneck: fewer than half of end-of-life electric-vehicle packs reach certified recyclers, with the rest exported, stockpiled, or lost to informal channels. Processing margins tightened as virgin lithium prices fell through the year. The review concludes that deposit-style return incentives and standardized pack designs would do more for supply than additional processing plants.'

expected_answer.summary: The 2026 Battery Recycling Market Review finds recycled lithium output doubled in 2025 and now meets 9 percent of regional battery-grade demand, but fewer than half of end-of-life EV packs reach certified recyclers. Falling virgin lithium prices squeezed processing margins. The review concludes that deposit-style return incentives and standardized pack designs matter more for supply than new processing plants.

Particulate matter declined only 6 percent, since much of it drifts in from construction, tire wear, and sources outside the zones. expected_answer.summary: The Metropolitan Air Quality Study 2025 found that low-emission zones cut nitrogen dioxide by 24 percent and children's asthma-related emergency visits by 11 percent across twelve cities. Particulate matter fell only 6 percent because much of it comes from construction, tire wear, and sources outside the zones. The authors recommend wider zone boundaries paired with construction-dust controls.
